scoped_knowledge:
This event is one of the earliest documented cases in the
dataset of a non-state-actor corporate compliance decision
cutting financial-infrastructure access on the basis of a
publisher's content. Three structural features make it
paper-relevant despite the pre-comparable-corpus date:

(a) The action is voluntary corporate policy, not a US
government enforcement action. No OFAC SDN designation
named WikiLeaks; no DOJ indictment or seizure order was
outstanding against WikiLeaks at 2010-12-07. Visa Europe's
stated rationale — investigation of whether the WikiLeaks
website "contravenes Visa operating rules" — is a
contractual / terms-of-service framing, not a legal-
compulsion framing.

(b) The action operates through a multi-tier acquirer chain:
Visa Europe (card network) → Teller A/S (Danish acquirer) →
Korta (Icelandic agent) → DataCell ehf (merchant). The
downstream merchant termination is the operational outcome,
but the upstream Visa Europe statement is what binds the
intermediate processors. The 2012 Reykjavík District Court
case is brought against Valitor hf, the post-Teller Iceland
processor, but the chain-of-causation reaches back to Visa
Europe's 2010-12-07 statement.

(c) The 2010-12 blockade is the empirical seed of the later
EU-competition-complaint thread (DataCell's 2011-08 / 2012-09
Article 101 / 102 EU competition complaint, the European
Parliament question E-007868/2013, and the resulting
Reykjavík District Court ruling in DataCell's favour on
2012-07-12). Treated as discovery_ledger_only because it
pre-dates the comparable-analysis corpus, but it is a
foundational anchor for the dataset's S5 corporate stratum.

The 2010-12 WikiLeaks financial blockade consisted of five legs
enumerated by the WikiLeaks Banking Blockade support-campaign page:
Bank of America (2010-12-18), PayPal (2010-12-04), MasterCard
(2010-12-07), VISA Europe (2010-12-07), and Western Union
(2010-12-21 addition to the Western Union Interdiction List).
This event records the Western Union leg.

Why null_event / null_case / coverage_gap with attribution=unknown:
this is the weakest-sourced leg of the blockade in the public
record located in this authoring pass. The PayPal, MasterCard,
VISA Europe, and Bank of America legs each carry primary corporate
disclosures (PayPal blog post, MasterCard wire statement, VISA
Europe press release, Bank of America press statement). The
Western Union leg is documented via the counterparty (WikiLeaks
itself, in its Banking Blockade support page) and contemporaneous
journalism (CSMonitor 2011-10-24, Forbes / Guardian coverage of
the blockade enumeration), but no primary Western Union corporate
press release explicitly announcing the addition of WikiLeaks to
the Interdiction List was located. Coding honestly: the cascade
is real but the primary acting-party evidence is missing, so the
load-bearing observation row is observation_kind=coverage_gap
with attribution=unknown, and the event admits at null_case /
null_event strength. Fabricating a primary URL or upgrading
attribution beyond what the public record supports would be
dishonest; the honest call is to record the gap.

Why discovery_only_2008_2012 tier: 2010 belongs to the pre-2013
discovery-only tier per sampling/frame.yaml. analysis_use=
discovery_ledger_only excludes this row from the 2017+ comparable-
analysis denominator and from the 2013-2016 historical-baseline
denominator. The event is retained as discovery-ledger material:
a pre-crypto-era corporate-policy money-transfer-rail closure
that produced the cross-rail cascade pattern later observable in
the comparable era. (The brief specified analysis_use=
discovery_only; the canonical schema enum is discovery_ledger_only
per sampling/frame.yaml. Used the canonical enum.)

Why offramp_cex coverage status=not_measured: Western Union is a
money-transfer operator rather than a crypto-asset CEX, but the
offramp_cex layer is the closest taxonomic match for a regulated
fiat money-transfer rail closure. The layer is marked not_measured
rather than partially_measured because no primary Western Union
disclosure was located and the WU leg is therefore not exchange-
side observable at primary-source strength. L0/L1/L3/L4/
asset_onchain are not_applicable on construct-did-not-exist or
construct-out-of-scope grounds.

Why related_events lists the four sibling WikiLeaks blockade
events: those events are companion records for the PayPal,
MasterCard, VISA Europe, and Bank of America legs of the same

scoped_knowledge:
This event sits in the discovery_only_2008_2012 tier as one of
five legs of the 2010-12 WikiLeaks financial blockade. The cross-
rail cascade pattern that the blockade exhibits — sequential cuts
by PayPal, MasterCard, VISA Europe, Bank of America, and Western
Union over a two-week window in response to WikiLeaks' publication
of US diplomatic cables — is a pre-crypto-era instance of the
same cascade-of-corporate-policy-actions shape that the
comparable-tier corpus documents in the crypto-asset off-ramp
layer (e.g. multi-exchange delistings, multi-issuer freezes).
The WU leg is the weakest-sourced of the five legs: the four
card / bank / payment-processor legs each carry primary corporate
disclosures, while the Western Union leg is attested only by
counterparty statement (WikiLeaks Banking Blockade page) and
contemporaneous journalism. Coding the WU leg honestly as
coverage_gap with attribution=unknown — rather than fabricating
a primary URL or upgrading attribution — preserves the cascade-
family completeness in the discovery ledger while accurately
representing the evidence-strength asymmetry across legs. The
~6-month gap between the WU action (2010-12-21) and WikiLeaks'
first acceptance of bitcoin donations (2011-06) is a candidate
recovery anchor for the family-level cascade but is not authored
as a separate recovery row in this event because the recovery
spans the family rather than the WU leg in isolation.
